builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: S1-Evo: Experience-Guided Evidence Competition Attacks on Typed System-1 Decision Models
summary: S1-Evo replaces generic prompt-injection or override attacks with contract-aware perturbations of untrusted fields that compete with task evidence against typed S1 scorers, using offline margin-guided search and retrieval of 'experience cards' at test time. Cost is an offline seed-task optimization loop with re-verification plus a card store and retrieval step at inference; it adds no parameters to the production model but adds attack-side compute and pipeline complexity. It can fail when margin feedback is unavailable or coarse-grained, when retrieved cards do not transfer to unseen task distributions, and when deployed S1 interfaces add input sanitization or contract validation not modeled by the framework.
rationale: For a small team deploying typed S1 routing, moderation, or authorization, this is primarily a red-teaming tool: worth testing against their own S1 interfaces to quantify injection risk, but not a defensive or performance improvement to adopt unconditionally.
technique: Experience-guided evidence-competition attacks on typed S1 models

claims.statement: S1-Evo replaces generic prompt-injection or override attacks with contract-aware perturbations of untrusted fields that compete with task evidence against typed S1 scorers, using offline margin-guided search and retrieval of 'experience cards' at test time. Cost is an offline seed-task optimization loop with re-verification plus a card store and retrieval step at inference; it adds no parameters to the production model but adds attack-side compute and pipeline complexity. It can fail when margin feedback is unavailable or coarse-grained, when retrieved cards do not transfer to unseen task distributions, and when deployed S1 interfaces add input sanitization or contract validation not modeled by the framework.
The paper reports 71.99% mean attack success rate and 57.47% high-confidence ASR on jev-1.14 across four benchmarks and three S1 models, plus up to 24.00% end-to-end agent violations.
